beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact thought process repeatedly reads and updates it before decoding.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The method separates the dense image field from the compact state that reasons over it. The encoder turns the low-resolution input into features that can carry spatial detail. Windowing partitions that field while preserving the tokens needed for reconstruction. DQ-CTM applies shared ticks to read and update the carrier. The decoder turns the updated carrier back into the super-resolved image. The recurrence returns to the DQ-CTM thought stage itself, with parameters shared across ticks.

params.headline: ThinkSR runs dense features through shared thought ticks
params.note: End to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder

beats.intent: The carrier is made by encoding the low-resolution image, then windowing the resulting dense feature field without dropping tokens.
beats.narration: The carrier equation makes the dense part of the method explicit. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into the feature field. The window partition operates on that field and keeps every token for the later thought process.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded first and windowed second

terms.label: encoder maps the low-resolution image to dense features

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the benchmark; its 1.129 million parameters are second largest among the five methods.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison does not support calling the method cheap. CATANet has the smallest count at zero point five three five million parameters. RFDN is slightly larger at zero point five five zero million. IMDN comes next at zero point seven one five million. DQ-CTM-SR is second largest at one point one two nine million.
